;Business and economy
*[[Amazon (company)|Amazon]] announces plans to open dozens of proprietary grocery stores in several major U.S. cities. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/amazon-to-launch-new-grocery-store-business-sources-say-11551461887 (''The Wall Street Journal'')],  [http://fortune.com/2019/03/01/amazon-may-launch-a-new-chain-of-grocery-stores/ (''Fortune'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*A bus overturns on the [[Qom]]–[[Tehran]] Highway in [[Iran]], killing eight people (including the driver) and injuring more than thirty others. Officials claim the driver fell asleep. [https://www.france24.com/en/20190301-8-dead-iran-bus-accident (France 24)]
*A [[Russia]]n cargo ship collides with a motorway bridge in the city of [[Busan]], [[South Korea]]. The captain is reported to be drunk. [https://www.theguardian.com/global/video/2019/mar/01/russian-cargo-ship-crashes-into-bridge-in-south-korea-video (''The Guardian'')]
*A leaking oil pipeline explodes in [[Bayelsa]], [[Nigeria]]; a stampede follows. Over 50 are reported missing. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/mar/02/more-than-50-missing-after-oil-pipeline-explosion-in-nigeria (''The Guardian'')]
*A BMW collides with two oncoming minibuses between [[Fouriesburg]] and [[Bethlehem, Free State|Bethlehem]] in [[Free State (province)|Free State]], [[South Africa]], killing thirteen and injuring eight. [https://ewn.co.za/2019/03/02/13-dead-8-injured-in-free-state-collision (Eyewitness News)]
;International relations
*[[Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh]]
**[[Bangladesh]]'s Foreign Secretary Shahidul Haque tells the [[United Nations Security Council]] that his country will no longer accept [[Rohingya people|Rohingya]] refugees fleeing violence across the border in [[Rakhine State]], and accuses [[Myanmar]] of "hollow promises" regarding [[repatriation]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-47412704 (BBC News)]
*[[North Korea–Vietnam relations]]
**[[List of leaders of North Korea|North Korean leader]] [[Kim Jong-un]] begins an official visit to [[Vietnam]], three days after arriving in the country for a nuclear summit with [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] that ended in deadlock. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/north-korean-leader-kim-jong-un-kicks-off-official-vietnam-visit (''The Straits Times'')]
*[[2019 Venezuelan presidential crisis]]
**The [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] announced Friday it is revoking the visas of 49 Maduro-aligned officials and their families and sanctioning several top military and security officials, part of a major U.S. campaign to push contested Venezuelan [[President of Venezuela|President]] [[Nicolás Maduro]] from power. [https://www.foxnews.com/politics/us-revokes-visas-of-49-maduro-aligned-officials-in-venezuela (Fox News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 United States presidential election]], [[2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries]]
**[[Governor of Washington|Washington Governor]] [[Jay Inslee]] announces he will join the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] primaries in 2020 and cites [[Climate change mitigation|fighting climate change]] as a reason. [http://time.com/5539302/jay-inslee-climate-change/ (''Time'')], [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/03/01/us/jay-inslee-2020.html (''The New York Times'')]
